questions

What owners ask us first.

SizeWhat size of company do you work with?Answer

We advise companies with $20M to $200M in revenue or enterprise value, across the Gulf’s lower and middle market. If you are smaller, talk to us anyway.

FeesHow do you charge?Answer

Fees are agreed for each mandate and set out in a written engagement letter before any work starts. We walk you through them on the first call.

MarketsWhich markets do you cover?Answer

Saudi Arabia and the UAE today, with the rest of the GCC next. Buyers and targets come from the US, Europe, China, India, Korea and other markets, through Translink member firms in 35+ countries.

AIWhat does your AI do, and who checks it?Answer

Blueprint AI reads your Arabic financials and documents and prepares buyer materials in each market’s language and format. A second layer ranks likely buyers from Translink research and our own list, so outreach starts in days. A DrawingBoard Capital advisor reviews every page and every approach.

TimingHow long does a sale take?Answer

Readiness takes 2–4 weeks. Once we launch, we aim to have offers within three months. Signing and completion then depend on negotiation, diligence and approvals.

ConfidentialityWill people find out we are selling?Answer

Buyers see an anonymous teaser first and only learn your name after signing an NDA. Your documents are handled under a confidentiality agreement.

LicensingAre you licensed to do this?Answer

DrawingBoard Capital provides strategic advisory, and the technology and AI services that make the M&A process faster and more efficient. Arranging a transaction and the sale of shares are carried out by licensed firms on both sides of the deal.

Your company, ready for buyers in their language.

Blueprint AI turns Arabic financials, memoranda and company documents into investor-ready materials for buyers in the US, UK, Europe and Asia, in the language and format each market expects.

Request early access →M&A advisory

the problem

Great Gulf companies, written for the wrong reader.

Most mid-market companies in Saudi Arabia and the UAE keep their records in Arabic, in local formats. International buyers want something else: their language, their structure, their definitions. The gap costs time, value and sometimes the deal.

  1. 01

    Your documents

    Arabic financial statements, management accounts, memoranda, contracts and board papers.

  2. 02

    Blueprint AI

    Our in-house AI translates, restructures and maps your information to each market’s format.

  3. 03

    Advisor review

    A DrawingBoard Capital advisor checks every page and every number before anything leaves the building.

  4. 04

    Investor packs

    A teaser, information memorandum and data-room index for each market you choose.

markets

One company. A pack for every buyer.

Not just translation. Each pack follows the presentation and reporting conventions used in that market, and is reviewed by an advisor before it is shared.

Home / Privacy policy

      

        
legal
Privacy policy

        
How DrawingBoard Capital collects, uses and protects the personal data you share through this website.
Effective 30 October 2026

      

    

  

  

    

        
1. Who we are

        
DrawingBoard Capital LLC (“DrawingBoard Capital”, “we”, “us”) is responsible for the personal data collected through this website. DrawingBoard Capital Gulf is a trading name of DrawingBoard Capital LLC, a company registered in the United States. If you have a question about this policy or your data, email albin@drawingboard.capital.

        
2. What we collect

        
We only collect what you choose to give us, and a small amount of technical information needed to run the website.

        
    
        
  • Mandate inquiries: your name, company, role, email, phone number, the type of inquiry, an approximate company value and your message.
    • 
        
  • Find Buyers and Market Comps: your company website, sector, country, revenue, EBITDA or profit, what you are looking to sell, your timing, your name, email and phone number, and whether you want a call.
    • 
        
  • Blueprint AI early access: your name, email, company, role, where the company is based and the languages you need.
    • 
        
  • Technical information: your browser stores your language choice so the site remembers it. Our hosting provider may keep standard server logs, such as IP address, browser type and the pages requested, for security and reliability.
    • 
        

        
Please do not send confidential company documents or financial statements through the website. We will ask for them separately, under a confidentiality agreement.

        
3. How we use it

        
    
        
  • To reply to your inquiry and arrange a call if you ask for one.
    • 
        
  • To prepare what you request, such as a first buyer list or a set of comparable deals.
    • 
        
  • To assess whether we can help and, if we agree to work together, to prepare an engagement letter.
    • 
        
  • To send you updates about your request and, only if you agree, other communications from DrawingBoard Capital.
    • 
        
  • To keep the website secure and meet our legal and regulatory obligations.
    • 
        

        
We rely on your consent, on steps you ask us to take before entering an engagement, on our legitimate interest in responding to business inquiries, and on our legal obligations. You can withdraw your consent at any time.

        
4. AI and automated tools

        
Information you enter into our tools may be processed with AI systems run by us or our technology providers to prepare buyer lists, comparables and materials. A DrawingBoard Capital advisor reviews this work before anything is sent to you. We do not make decisions about you based solely on automated processing.

        
5. Who we share it with

        
    
        
  • Service providers who host the website, run our CRM and email, or provide AI and data tools, under contracts that protect your data.
    • 
        
  • Translink Corporate Finance member firms, only where needed for your request and with your agreement.
    • 
        
  • Potential buyers, investors or counterparties, only on your instruction and under a confidentiality agreement.
    • 
        
  • Professional advisers, regulators, courts or authorities where the law requires it.
    • 
        

        
We do not sell your personal data.

        
6. International transfers

        
Some of our service providers and Translink member firms are outside Saudi Arabia, the UAE and the European Economic Area. When your data is transferred abroad, we use the safeguards the applicable law requires, such as contractual protections.

        
7. How long we keep it

        
We keep inquiry data for up to 24 months after our last contact with you, unless you ask us to delete it sooner. If you become a client, we keep records for as long as the engagement and the law require.

        
8. Your rights

        
Depending on where you live, including under Saudi Arabia’s Personal Data Protection Law, the UAE’s Personal Data Protection Law and the EU and UK GDPR, you can ask to:

        
    
        
  • access the personal data we hold about you and receive a copy;
    • 
        
  • correct data that is wrong or incomplete;
    • 
        
  • delete your data, or restrict or object to how we use it;
    • 
        
  • withdraw your consent, without affecting what we did before you withdrew it.
    • 
        

        
To use any of these rights, email albin@drawingboard.capital. You can also complain to your data protection authority, such as the Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA), the UAE Data Office, or your local authority in the EU or UK.

        
9. Cookies and browser storage

        
This website does not use advertising or tracking cookies. It stores one setting in your browser to remember your language. If we add analytics, we will update this policy and ask for your consent where the law requires it.

        
10. Security

        
We use reasonable technical and organisational measures to protect your data. No website or transmission over the internet is completely secure.

        
11. Children

        
This website is for business owners and professionals. It is not meant for anyone under 18, and we do not knowingly collect their data.

        
12. Changes to this policy

        
We may update this policy. The date at the top shows when it last changed.

      insights

            DrawingBoard CapitalM&A · 3 min read
            What a buyer’s diligence finds first.
            Five issues that cost sellers price or time, and why it pays to find them before the buyer does.
            Read the note
          
          
      
            
      Most value lost in a sale is lost in diligence, not in the first offer. The issues are rarely new to the owner. They are new to the buyer, and that is what costs money.
      
            
        
              
      1. Revenue quality. How much is recurring, and how much depends on a handful of customers.
        2. 
              
      2. Working capital. What a normal level looks like, because the price adjusts against it at completion.
        3. 
              
      3. Add-backs. Adjustments to profit that do not survive a second look.
        4. 
              
      4. Contracts. Change-of-control clauses with customers, suppliers and landlords.
        5. 
              
      5. Key people. How much of the business walks out with the founder.
        6. 
            
      
            
      None of these is a reason not to sell. Each is a reason to prepare. That is the point of Transaction Readiness: a valuation range, the issues list and a straight answer on timing, before a buyer sees anything.
      
          
      
        
      

        
      
          
            DrawingBoard CapitalCo-advisory · 2 min read
            Two advisors, one mandate.
            How co-advisory works when it works: who leads, who owns the client, and what gets agreed up front.
            Read the note
          
          
      
            
      Co-advisory fails for one reason: roles agreed late. It works when three things are written down before the first call.
      
            
        
              
      1. Who leads. One advisor runs the process and speaks to the client.
        2. 
              
      2. Who owns the relationship. The client stays with the advisor who brought them, during and after the deal.
        3. 
              
      3. Who does what. Buyer reach, materials, negotiation and closing, split before work starts.
        4. 
            
      
            
      Done this way, the client gets more reach and one voice, and both advisors get a deal neither would have closed alone. More on our Partners page.
